items.abstract: <jats:p>Coastal wetlands provide critical ecosystem services yet face increasing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) contamination, and comparison of wetland microbiome responses to PFAS remains poorly resolved. Laboratory-enriched microbial consortia derived from freshwater marsh and salt marsh soils were exposed to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in 75-day microcosms at 0, 1, and 10 mg/L, then characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, phylogenetic null modeling, neutral community modeling, and KEGG-level functional prediction. Both enriched consortia showed a modest decrease in aqueous PFOA (~11–13%) at 1 mg/L but not at 10 mg/L, consistent with a potential contribution from biosorption-mediated immobilization. Incubation time dominated beta-diversity shifts (ANOSIM R > 0.90, p = 0.001), while PFOA produced no detectable compositional separation. Exploratory additive mixed-effects models indicated that alpha diversity varied primarily with microbial community source and sampling day, whereas PFOA concentration showed a nominal overall association only with Shannon diversity. Assembly analyses showed that PFOA was associated with stronger heterogeneous selection in the salt-marsh-derived consortium, whereas the freshwater-derived consortium remained stochastically dominated. When PFOA-exposed samples were pooled across both enriched consortia, the neutral community model fit collapsed (R2 < 0), signaling a regime shift toward deterministic, PFOA-mediated selection. Functionally, the salt-marsh-derived consortium showed predicted enrichment in taurine/hypotaurine metabolism and broad-spectrum proteolytic functions (serralysin and creatinase), whereas the freshwater-marsh-derived consortium showed predicted enrichment in glutathione metabolism, xenobiotic dioxygenase functions, and DNA repair pathways. Candidate PFOA-sensitive (Pseudohongiella, Flavobacterium, Parvibaculum) and PFOA-tolerant (Sericytochromatia, Legionella) taxa were identified as source-associated candidate biomarkers. Under the tested culture conditions, PFOA responses differed between the laboratory-enriched freshwater-marsh- and salt-marsh-derived bacterial consortia. These results describe source-associated responses of the enriched consortia but may need further validation with native wetland communities.</jats:p>
title: Microbial Responses to PFOA in Coastal Wetland: An Ecological Comparison Between Freshwater and Salt Marsh

items.abstract: <jats:p>Understanding microplastic (MP) transport dynamics in river systems requires spatially and temporally resolved monitoring to disentangle localized point sources from diffuse catchment inputs. This study investigated MP contamination across two contrasting Central European catchments: the heavily impounded, industrialized Neckar (n = 136; June 2026) and the transboundary Lusatian Neisse (n = 102; March and May 2026). A standardized monitoring campaign collected 0.5 L grab samples across both rivers and at the Neckar–Rhine confluence in Mannheim, including an inland port area, where 12 sites were sampled on four dates between January and April 2026. Samples underwent hydrogen peroxide digestion, fluorescent staining with a MP-specific dye mixture (particles > 10 µm), automated fluorescence microscopy, and geospatial analysis incorporating land cover and wastewater infrastructure metrics. Microplastic concentrations were significantly higher in the Neisse than in the Neckar (median 22.5 vs. 5.0 MP L−1; Cliff’s delta = 0.44). Because the two rivers were sampled in different months and at different water levels, seasonal and hydrological contributions to this difference cannot be excluded. In the Mannheim port area, the highest site mean was recorded upstream of a lock structure (544 MP L−1) with pronounced temporal variability at this site (5 to 1591 MP L−1). Neither local land use nor wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) metrics showed a detectable association with MP abundances in either river under the present design, which could reliably detect only moderate to strong associations. These results indicate that immediate land cover and WWTP proximity left no detectable signal in surface-water MP concentrations, possibly because point-source signals are masked by diffuse inputs, hydrological dynamics and temporal variation. Concentrations in the Neisse decreased from the upper to the lower reaches; whether this reflects the secondary WWTPs of the upper catchment or other longitudinal differences (e.g., flow conditions) could not be resolved.</jats:p>
title: Catchment-Specific Drivers of Microplastic Contamination in Two Central European Rivers: A Citizen Science Monitoring Campaign Along the Neckar and the Lusatian Neisse

items.abstract: <jats:p>The co-pyrolysis of corncob (CC) and water hyacinth (WH) was investigated to characterize their thermal decomposition behavior, kinetic properties, and resulting biochars. Thermogravimetric (TGA) and derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) analyses were conducted at heating rates of 5 and 20 °C min−1 for the individual feedstocks and their blends. Biochars from CC, WH, and CC50:WH50 were produced at 350 °C and characterized for physicochemical properties. At 5 °C min−1, apparent activation energies estimated using the Coats–Redfern method were 135.4, 73.2, 83.1, 96.4, and 103.6 kJ mol−1 for CC, WH, CC30:WH70, CC50:WH50, respectively. Experimental and theoretical thermogravimetric profiles were compared to assess deviations from additive behavior. Biochar yields ranged from 39.22% to 46.17%, while mean pH values ranged from 9.34 to 9.56. One-way analysis of variance indicated significant treatment differences in yield, electrical conductivity, total nitrogen, available phosphorus, cation exchange capacity, and bulk density, whereas pH differences were not significant. WH biochar exhibited the highest electrical conductivity, total nitrogen, and available phosphorus, while CC50:WH50 had the highest cation exchange capacity and bulk density. These findings show that feedstock composition influences thermal behavior and biochar properties.</jats:p>
title: Thermo-Kinetic Analysis of Corncob-Water Hyacinth Co-Pyrolysis for Synergistic Insights and Biochar Characteristics for Soil Amendment

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigated the emission inventory and reduction strategies of non-road construction machinery in Tangshan Port. A Portable Emission Measurement System (PEMS) was used to collect operating condition data and measure pollutant emissions from 16 pieces of machinery under real-world operating conditions. Based on the field measurements, emission factors for typical construction machinery in Tangshan Port were established. The emission reduction effects and cost-effectiveness of different scenarios of phase-out and Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) emission control ratios for China III emission standard non-road construction machinery at Tangshan Port were analyzed. The results showed that the estimated annual operating hours of excavators, loaders, forklifts, and bulldozers in the port were 3.51, 4.87, 3.44, and 2.34 times the corresponding values recommended in the “Technical Guidelines for the Compilation of Emission Inventories of Non-road Mobile Pollution Sources (Trial)”, respectively, indicating relatively high utilization intensity. Emissions of PM, NOx, HC, and CO from port construction machinery were mainly attributable to excavators and loaders, with combined contribution rates of 66.65%, 68.58%, 60.89%, and 59.85%, respectively. For China III emission standard machinery, the combined phase-out and DPF retrofit strategies showed that, for every 10% increase in the phase-out ratio, the average annual investment in emission control increased by RMB 98 million (converted at the current exchange rate, it is approximately: USD 14.58 million and EUR 13.02 million), the average annual NOx reduction increased by 85.5 tons, whereas the average annual PM reduction increased by 2.5 tons.</jats:p>
title: Research on Emission Inventory and Emission Reduction Benefits Assessment of Non-Road Construction Machinery in Tangshan Port

items.abstract: <jats:p>Meteorology drives the day-to-day pollution variation behind short-term health effects, and its misattribution biases exposure estimates and trend normalisation. Wind speed and boundary-layer height (BLH), the main dispersion variables, are strongly collinear (mean r ≈ 0.70, 0.81 on anomalies), with contested relative roles. We quantified their unique variances with semi-partial R2 for NO2, O3, PM10 and PM2.5 in France’s 10 largest cities (2018–2025), across four frames, from pooled levels to deseasonalised, de-trended anomalies, checked with generalised additive models and for wind direction. On pooled levels, BLH carries on average four times the unique variance of wind for NO2 and O3, and eight to ten for particulate matter, whereas their raw correlations with primary pollutants differ only 1.3- to 1.4-fold. This lead is robust for particulate matter, even with direction controlled. For O3, temperature dominates and humidity exceeds BLH on average, plausibly a photochemical signal. For NO2 it is partly seasonal: on anomalies they become comparable, and wind leads significantly only where regional winds are coherent. The NO2 contrasts define three city types, wind-dominated, transitional and BLH-dominated. Both remain significant for NO2 anomalies in every city, so normalisation models should retain both, with city-specific coefficients. BLH should become a first-tier predictor.</jats:p>
title: Boundary-Layer Height Outweighs Wind Speed in Explaining Daily Urban Air Pollution: Unique-Variance Attribution and a City Typology for 10 French Cities

items.abstract: <jats:p>Urban surface deposited sediments are important reservoirs of pollutants, yet their relationships with other environmental media and their value for distinguishing legacy contamination from current anthropogenic inputs remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the urban sediment cascade across eight industrial cities in Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia. The study combines geochemical data for urban soils from regional monitoring with analyses of urban surface deposited sediments, their fine fraction (<0.1 mm), and snow cover. Concentrations of Mg, Mn, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, Sb, and Pb in the sediment cascade strata were considered. An initial geochemical baseline was reconstructed using principal component analysis and non-parametric Kernel density estimation. Pollution was assessed using geochemically justified element-specific pollution index and an integrated toxicity-weighted pollution index. The multi-strata profiling and analysis of eco-geochemical spectra successfully isolated key trajectories of technogenic transformation, including post-industrial legacy, continuous metallurgical complexes pressure, mining impacts, and climate-dependent transboundary transit. The toxicity-weighted pollution assessment classified 54% of sampling sites as heavily or severely polluted. The developed approach provides a universally scalable methodology for multi-temporal environmental monitoring within industrial and post-industrial urban areas.</jats:p>
title: Urban Sediment Cascade as Geochemical Archive: Tracking Industrial Impact and Pollution in Urban Environment

items.abstract: <jats:p>Conventional wastewater treatment processes are not specifically designed to efficiently eliminate pharmaceutical contaminants such as metronidazole (MTZ), highlighting the need for effective advanced oxidation processes (AOPs). Heterogeneous persulfate activation represents a promising approach for degrading recalcitrant organic pollutants. In this study, Cu-loaded activated tire char (ATC-Cu) catalysts were synthesized for the first time using different ATC/Cu weight percentages (2.5, 5, and 10% w/w) and evaluated for MTZ degradation through peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and peroxydisulfate (PDS) activation. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of the Cu2O crystal phase, while textural characterization revealed a meso–macroporous structure. Among the investigated systems, ATC-10 w/w Cu/PMS exhibited the highest catalytic performance, achieving complete MTZ degradation within 10 min, with an apparent kinetic rate constant of k = 0.357 min−1. The optimum PMS and catalyst dosages were 250 and 400 mg/L, respectively. Mechanistic investigations identified SO4•− as the dominant reactive species, indicating a predominantly radical oxidation pathway, whereas •OH played a secondary role. The influence of inorganic ions and natural organic matter was also evaluated, revealing limited inhibition of MTZ degradation. Overall, ATC-Cu catalysts combine efficient persulfate activation with waste-tire valorization, demonstrating their potential as sustainable catalysts for pharmaceutical-contaminated wastewater treatment.</jats:p>
title: Cu2O/Waste Tire-Derived Activated Carbon Catalysts Applied in Persulfate Oxidation Processes for Antibiotic Remediation in Aqueous Matrices
